scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Swing dance originated in the 1920s within African-American communities in the United States, particularly in Harlem, New York.
The Savoy Ballroom was central to this development, fostering a fusion of jazz-based movements that resulted in the Lindy Hop.
Over the following decades, the dance evolved into various regional and stylistic forms, spreading across the U.S. and eventually to Europe.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Swing is a social dance, though it has developed a significant competitive culture.
It is used for recreation, community building, and artistic expression.
In some contexts, it is a competitive sport with standardized judging criteria.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Swing Dance.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2f/Swing_Dance.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Swing dances are generally performed in pairs, though solo variations exist.
The technique typically involves a 'bounce' or rhythmic compression into the floor.
Basic steps are often counted in six or eight-beat patterns.
Watch for Swingout.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (LQxHfEjBhh0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular or slotted (linear) depending on the specific style.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Swing dance is danced to swing-style jazz, characterized by a ternary rhythm (12/8 feel) that gives the music a 'bouncing' quality.
Instrumentation typically includes brass sections (trumpets, trombones, saxophones) and a rhythm section (drums, bass, piano, guitar).
Listen for the Brass section, Drums, Double bass, Piano.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 185 beats a minute.
Recognizable by a driving, syncopated rhythm section and a 'swing' feel where the eighth notes are unequal, creating a forward-moving, bouncy energy.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Historically associated with dance halls and juke joints, swing is now performed in studios, clubs, and competition venues.
There is no specific costume, though comfortable, durable clothing and shoes that allow for movement and sliding are standard.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Frankie Manning, George Snowden, Dean Collins, and Hal Takier are key figures historically associated with the development and preservation of swing dance styles.
Variants include the Lindy Hop (Harlem), Balboa (Southern California), Collegiate Shag (Carolinas), West Coast Swing (California), and Swing Criollo (Costa Rica).

Swing dance is rooted in African-American vernacular dance traditions, influenced by jazz music, and has since branched into numerous derivatives including Jive, Boogie-Woogie, and modern competitive forms.
